extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and novelists (especially those who want to strengthen conflict and suspense; thriller writers, writing students, and revising authors)
extracted.subtask_short: writing conflict and suspense in fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for crafting and revising scenes, characters, point of view, and plot elements so that conflict and suspense drive a novel from first word to last. Focus is on techniques to heighten tension, balance pacing devices, and keep readers engaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pack the beginning, middle, and end of your book with the right amount of conflict.
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure each major structural section (beginning, middle, end) contains appropriate and escalating conflict so the story remains compelling across its arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ramp up the tension and keep readers hooked; use conflict strategically at each structural phase to move plot forward and sustain engagement. Avoid sections that are low on conflict or that drop tension unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tap into the suspenseful power of each character’s inner conflict.
rubrics_metrics.description: Use characters' internal struggles to generate suspense and emotional stakes, not only external plot obstacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make inner conflict relevant to plot decisions and reveal it in ways that raise questions and uncertainty, increasing readers' investment and suspense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build conflict into your story’s point of view.
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage POV choices to create or intensify conflict—what the narrator/POV character knows, hides, or misunderstands affects suspense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use limited or unreliable POV strategically to withhold or reveal information; let POV decisions generate dramatic irony or uncertainty that sustains suspense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance subplots, flashbacks, and backstory to keep your story moving forward.
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate secondary storylines and past material so they support rather than stall the main conflict and plot momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overloading with backstory or tangential subplots; ensure every subplot or flashback advances theme, character, or raises stakes to maintain forward motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize the tension in your characters’ dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.description: Make dialogue a source of conflict and suspense by packing it with subtext, obstacles, and competing intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use confrontations, evasions, revealing slips, and withheld information in dialogue to heighten tension; avoid exposition-heavy or neutral dialogue that dissipates suspense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amp up the suspense when you revise.
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat revision as an active stage to increase tension, tighten scenes, and heighten stakes across the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During revision, look for opportunities to raise stakes, shorten scenes that sag, sharpen conflict beats, and reorder or prune material to sustain suspense; revision is where much suspense is created.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft scenes, create characters, and develop storylines that harness conflict and suspense to carry your story from the first word to the last.
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall craft goal: every scene, character arc, and plotline should contribute to the ongoing pressure and uncertainty that propel the reader forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design scenes with clear conflict goals, ensure characters' desires and obstacles create tension, and align storylines so their intersections amplify suspense throughout the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from examples of successful novels and movies.
rubrics_metrics.description: Study exemplary works to see how conflict and suspense are structured and executed in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze models to identify techniques you can emulate—how scenes are built, how revelations are timed, how POV and pacing create tension—and apply those patterns to your own revision and drafting.
